4. What Management Did Right vs. Wrong & Earnings Call Q&A Audit

✅ What Management Did Right (Operational Tailwinds)

  • 500-Truck Charger Logistics MOU: Secured a massive DaaS commitment for 500 trucks along the Dallas-to-Laredo artery, unlocking hundreds of millions in long-term pipeline.
  • Safety & Utilization Milestone: Surpassed 500,000 commercial driverless miles with zero safety incidents and a 100% on-time delivery record.
  • Federal Regulatory Alignment: Leveraged USDOT's AV National Strategy and FMCSA's 5-year warning beacon exemption to solidify interstate operational certainty.
  • Balance Sheet Fortress: Preserved $1.03B in total liquidity ($1,034M in cash & short-term investments), providing full runway through 2027 commercial deployment.

⚠️ What Management Did Wrong (Execution Headwinds)

  • Roush Manufacturing Ramp Delay: Acknowledged a 6-week delay in weekly truck production due to material availability and component testing bottlenecks.
  • FY26 Revenue Realignment: Lowered full-year revenue expectation to ~$9M (from ~$10M prior consensus) due to the delayed manufacturing curve.
  • Q4 Cash Burn Surge: Guided Q4 cash use to approximately $250M, accelerating cash outflow to resolve Roush production bottlenecks.
  • ATM Share Dilution: Issued 6 million Class A shares under the ATM equity facility for $41M net proceeds to fund RSU tax liabilities.

Institutional Conference Call & Analyst Q&A Forensic Highlights (Hardest Analyst Questions)

Mark Delaney (Goldman Sachs) • Topic: Charger Logistics 500-Truck MOU & DaaS Economic Model

Analyst Question: "Chris, the 500-truck commitment with Charger Logistics is significant. Can you walk through the revenue recognition cadence for these trucks between 2027 and 2028, and how the DaaS per-mile fee structure scales relative to your initial TaaS model?"

Executive Response: "CEO Chris Urmson explained that the Charger Logistics MOU transitions Aurora from capital-intensive fleet ownership (TaaS) to asset-light software licensing (DaaS). Charger will own and maintain the trucks, paying Aurora an ongoing software subscription and per-mile autonomy utilization fee. Delivery will phase across 2027 and 2028 along the Dallas-to-Laredo corridor, delivering high-margin recurring software revenues and unlocking hundreds of millions in cumulative value."

George Gianarikas (Canaccord Genuity) • Topic: Roush 6-Week Manufacturing Lag & Component Quality Resolution

Analyst Question: "David, you cited a six-week delay in the manufacturing ramp at Roush due to material availability and end-of-line testing. Are those component shortages fully behind you now, and what gives you confidence in achieving 20 trucks per week by early December?"

Executive Response: "CFO David Maday and VP Brad Rzetelny confirmed that the initial bottlenecks were related to specialized harness connectors and sensor calibration fixtures during initial line bring-up. The engineering team redesigned the testing protocols, all tooling is now validated, and the facility is running 16 hours a day with validated inventory on-site, providing complete confidence in hitting the 20-trucks-per-week run rate in early December."

Brian Ossenbeck (JPMorgan) • Topic: Federal AV Regulatory Framework & FMCSA Warning Beacon Exemption

Analyst Question: "Chris, could you elaborate on the regulatory progress with USDOT's Automated Vehicles National Strategy and the recent FMCSA five-year exemption for cab-mounted warning beacons?"

Executive Response: "Chris Urmson emphasized that federal regulatory momentum is inflecting positively. The FMCSA five-year exemption formally validates that cab-mounted automated beacons eliminate roadside hazards for commercial drivers. Furthermore, Secretary Sean Duffy and the Trump Administration's AV National Strategy establish federal safety standards and corridor interoperability, providing regulatory certainty that reinforces Aurora's multi-state commercial rollout."
